text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Protests against Social Affairs Minister Lore Hostasch's plans to reform the pension system to save some 16 billion schillings for the government are increasing as trade unions demand to see figures.
- The conservative People's Party urges the Social Affairs Ministry to reform the whole pension system and not only provide single budget measures.
- Milk producer NOeM plans to cut 140 jobs in a bid to compensate for losses.
- The government's plans to subsidise technological research and development will have to be redrawn after the government's meeting in Rust last week.
- Papermaker Laakirchen's dividend for 1996 will remain constant at 10 schillings. Even though prices were down, the operating profit was up 331 million schillings to 575 million schillings.
- Vienna's energy provider Wiener Stadtwerke has entered a bid for Upper Austria's energy provider OKA.
- Roadbuilder Teerag-Asdag raised its dividend up two schillings to 12 schillings as pre-tax profits rose to 40.3 million schillings from 30 million.
- GiroCredit's textile making subsidiary Eybl Krems Textilwerke plans to go public in April 1998.
- Andreas Goldberger, former ski-jumping world champion, has left the national team after his suspension because of his use of cocaine.
DIE PRESSE
- High income earners will be worst hit by the government's plans to restructure the public pension system.
- GiroCredit wants to take over the majority of builder Rogner as bank creditors will have to inject 500 million schillings into the building group. Rogner himself has denied any problems, however.
- Telephone providers and the industry are heavily criticising the telecommunications agency's plan to change area codes ahead of market liberalisation.
- The government should pay for the costs of installing bugging facilities which telephone companies will have to provide.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Former Chancellor Franz Vranitzky is rumoured to be a possible candidate to be in charge of the European Unions's foreign policy.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Insurance holding BARC is considering splitting business among its subsidiaries.
- Companies Topcall and Schoeller-Bleckmann Oilfield are the first Austrian companies to be listed at Brussel's EASDAQ stock exchange.
- A consortium including papermaker Frantschach is said to be the top-candidate to take over Poland's largest paper producer Celuloza.
- Voest Alpine subsidiaries MCE and Elin have received the oredr to build a turbine production facility worth 170 million schillings.
